Overview China has one of the most advanced mobile payment ecosystems in the world. Over 90% of daily transactions are made via QR codes, and cash is becoming increasingly rare. As a foreign visitor, you have multiple convenient options to pay for everything from street food to luxury shopping. Payment Methods Comparison Method Setup Time Fees Coverage Best For Alipay + Foreign Card 15 min 3% (over ¥200/day) ★★★★★ Most travelers WeChat Pay + Foreign Card 15 min 3% (over ¥200/day) ★★★★★ Social + payments Tour Card (UnionPay) 10 min 5% top-up fee ★★★★☆ Budget travelers e-CNY (Digital Yuan) 10 min 0% ★★★☆☆ Tech-savvy visitors PayPal (US users) 0 min Varies ★★★★☆ US travelers Cash 0 min Exchange fees ★★★☆☆ Backup only Alipay Setup Guide What You Need

Step-by-Step Setup Pro Tip: Set up Alipay at home before your trip. Verification servers work best on international internet connections. 1. Download Alipay from the App Store or Google Play. Make sure to download the official app by Ant Group. 2. Sign up with your phone number (foreign numbers work). Select your country code and enter your number. 3. Verify your phone by entering the SMS code sent to you. 4. Add your bank card: Go to "Me" → "Bank Cards" → "Add Card". Enter your international credit card details (Visa, Mastercard, American Express, JCB, Diners Club, or Discover). 5. Complete 3D Secure verification with your card issuer. Important: Enable "international online purchases" and "3D Secure" with your bank before traveling — this prevents 90% of binding failures. 6. Verify your identity (recommended): Upload your passport photo and complete facial recognition. This increases your annual spending limit from $2,000 to $50,000. Fees & Limits

How to Pay There are two ways to pay with Alipay:

WeChat Pay Setup Guide What You Need

Step-by-Step Setup 1. Download WeChat (Weixin) from the App Store or Google Play. Use the international version. 2. Sign up with your foreign mobile number. Select your region and enter your phone number. 3. Verify your phone with the SMS code. Create a WeChat password. 4. Set language to English (if needed): Go to Me → Settings → General → Language → English. 5. Add your bank card: Go to "Me" → "Services" → "Wallet" → "Cards" → "Add a Card". Enter your international credit card details. 6. Complete verification: Follow the prompts to verify your identity and card. You may need to upload your passport. New User Bonus: First-time users who bind an international card enjoy 90 days of fee-free payments (daily ¥200 limit waived) starting from May 2026. Fees & Limits

WeChat Pay vs Alipay Both are widely accepted and work similarly. The main difference is that WeChat is primarily a social messaging app with payments built in, while Alipay is focused on finance and shopping. Most travelers set up both for maximum coverage. Tour Card (UnionPay) What is Tour Card? How to Apply Tour Card is a prepaid virtual card designed specifically for foreign visitors to China. It is issued by UnionPay and works at all merchants that accept UnionPay QR codes. Key Features

How to Apply via UnionPay App 1. Download the UnionPay (云闪付) app from App Store or Google Play 2. Register with your passport and phone number 3. Search for "Tour Card" on the home page 4. Fill in your information and upload passport photo 5. Top up your card with your international credit card Alternative: Nihao China App Launched in late 2025, Nihao China is a dedicated app for foreigners that combines payment, transportation, translation, and travel services. You can also apply for Tour Card through this app with email, Apple ID, or foreign phone number registration. Fees & Limits

Note: Tour Card has weaker coverage at small street vendors compared to Alipay and WeChat Pay. It works best at formal merchants, restaurants, supermarkets, and tourist attractions. Digital Yuan (e-CNY) What is e-CNY? Setup Guide e-CNY (Digital Yuan) is China official central bank digital currency (CBDC). It is the simplest payment option for foreigners because it requires no Chinese phone number, no Chinese bank account, and charges zero transaction fees. Key Advantages

Setup Guide 1. Download the e-CNY app (数字人民币 试点版) from App Store or Google Play 2. Register with your phone number — select your country code and enter your foreign phone number 3. Open a wallet — choose any major Chinese bank (Bank of China, ICBC, etc.). They all work the same for tourists. 4. Top up your wallet with Visa or Mastercard 5. Start paying — scan merchant QR codes or use tap-to-pay via NFC Hong Kong Visitors: FPS Top-up If you are traveling from Hong Kong, you can top up your e-CNY wallet using Hong Kong FPS (Fast Payment System / 转数快):

Good to know: e-CNY acceptance is growing but not as universal as Alipay or WeChat Pay. It works best in major cities and pilot areas including Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, Shenzhen, and other pilot regions. PayPal in China (2026 Update) How It Works In May 2026, Tencent announced that TenPay Global (WeChat Pay international arm) has officially integrated with PayPal World. This is a game-changer for international travelers, especially US visitors. What Changed? Before May 2026: PayPal could not be used to pay at Chinese shops, restaurants, or taxis. Travelers had to set up Alipay or WeChat Pay, or carry cash. From May 2026: PayPal users can pay directly at millions of WeChat Pay merchants across China by scanning QR codes — no new app, no new account, no identity verification needed. How It Works 1. Open your existing PayPal app — no need to download WeChat or Alipay 2. Scan the merchant WeChat Pay QR code using PayPal scanner 3. Enter the amount and confirm payment 4. Funds come directly from your PayPal account — merchant receives Chinese yuan Alternatively, you can show your PayPal-generated QR code for the merchant to scan. Availability

Why this is great: Zero setup required — just use your existing PayPal account. No identity verification, no passport upload, no learning new apps. Perfect for short trips or if you have trouble setting up Alipay/WeChat. Cash & International Cards Cash International Credit Cards Cash While China is rapidly becoming cashless, cash is still legal tender and businesses are required by law to accept it. However, many smaller vendors may not have change, and some services (food delivery, ride-hailing apps) are app-only. Getting Cash

Tips for Using Cash

International Credit Cards International credit cards (Visa, Mastercard, American Express) have limited acceptance in China. They work mainly at international hotels, large department stores, and tourist-oriented businesses — roughly 30% of physical merchants. Where Cards Work

Pro Tip: Link your international card to Alipay or WeChat Pay instead of using it directly. This gives you access to 95%+ of merchants instead of just 30%. The 3% fee is well worth the convenience. Practical Tips Before You Go

During Your Trip

Transportation

Online Services

FAQ Q: Do I need a Chinese phone number? A: No. All major payment apps (Alipay, WeChat Pay, e-CNY) support foreign phone numbers. However, having a Chinese SIM card can make things easier, especially for other services like food delivery. Q: Do I need a Chinese bank account? A: No. You can link your international credit card directly to Alipay, WeChat Pay, or use Tour Card / e-CNY. No Chinese bank account is required for short-term visits. Q: Which is better: Alipay or WeChat Pay? A: Both are widely accepted and work almost identically. Most travelers set up both for maximum coverage. Alipay is slightly more finance/shopping focused, while WeChat is social-first with payments built in. Q: What if my card binding fails? A: Try these solutions:

Q: Is it safe to use mobile payments in China? A: Yes, mobile payments in China are extremely secure. They use multiple layers of encryption, biometric authentication (fingerprint, face ID), and real-time fraud monitoring. Millions of people use them every day without issues. Q: Can I get a refund if I have leftover balance? A: Yes, for most services:

Q: What about tax refunds? A: Some cities (like Hangzhou, Shenzhen) offer tax refund services for foreign visitors. Look for "Tax Refund" signs at participating stores. You can usually get the refund at the airport when leaving China, or in some cases, instant refund in-store. Q: Can I use Apple Pay or Google Pay? A: Apple Pay and Google Pay have very limited acceptance in China. They work only at a small number of merchants that support contactless international card payments. You are much better off using Alipay or WeChat Pay. Recommended Plan For Most Travelers (1-2 weeks) 1. Set up Alipay + WeChat Pay with your international credit card before departure. This gives you near-universal coverage. 2. Carry ¥300-500 cash as backup for taxis, small stalls, or situations where QR payments fail. 3. Verify your identity on at least one platform to increase your spending limit. For Budget Travelers If you want to minimize fees:

For US Travelers US visitors have an extra option:

For Longer Stays (1+ month) If you are staying longer: 1. Consider opening a Chinese bank account for lower fees and full functionality 2. Get a Chinese phone number for easier access to all services 3. Complete full identity verification on all payment platforms Bottom Line: Set up Alipay before your trip, bring some cash as backup, and you will be able to pay for almost anything in China just like a local. The process takes about 15 minutes and is well worth the convenience.

- International credit card (Visa, Mastercard, Amex, JCB, Diners Club, Discover)
- Passport (for identity verification)
- Phone number (foreign number works)

- Transactions over ¥200 per day: 3% service fee

- Show your payment code: Tap "Pay" to display your QR code, let the cashier scan it. This is faster and more common in stores.

Set language to English (if needed): Go to Me → Settings → General → Language → English. 5. Add your bank card: Go to "Me" → "Services" → "Wallet" → "Cards" → "Add a Card". Enter your international credit card details. 6. Complete verification: Follow the prompts to verify your identity and card. You may need to upload your passport. New User Bonus: First-time users who bind an international card enjoy 90 days of fee-free payments (daily ¥200 limit waived) starting from May 2026. Fees & Limits

The main difference is that WeChat is primarily a social messaging app with payments built in, while Alipay is focused on finance and shopping. Most travelers set up both for maximum coverage. Tour Card (UnionPay) What is Tour Card? How to Apply Tour Card is a prepaid virtual card designed specifically for foreign visitors to China. It is issued by UnionPay and works at all merchants that accept UnionPay QR codes. Key Features

How to Apply via UnionPay App 1. Download the UnionPay (云闪付) app from App Store or Google Play 2. Register with your passport and phone number 3. Search for "Tour Card" on the home page 4. Fill in your information and upload passport photo 5. Top up your card with your international credit card Alternative: Nihao China App Launched in late 2025, Nihao China is a dedicated app for foreigners that combines payment, transportation, translation, and travel services. You can also apply for Tour Card through this app with email, Apple ID, or foreign phone number registration. Fees & Limits

Note: Tour Card has weaker coverage at small street vendors compared to Alipay and WeChat Pay. It works best at formal merchants, restaurants, supermarkets, and tourist attractions. Digital Yuan (e-CNY) What is e-CNY? Setup Guide e-CNY (Digital Yuan) is China official central bank digital currency (CBDC). It is the simplest payment option for foreigners because it requires no Chinese phone number, no Chinese bank account, and charges zero transaction fees. Key Advantages

Open a wallet — choose any major Chinese bank (Bank of China, ICBC, etc.). They all work the same for tourists. 4. Top up your wallet with Visa or Mastercard 5. Start paying — scan merchant QR codes or use tap-to-pay via NFC Hong Kong Visitors: FPS Top-up If you are traveling from Hong Kong, you can top up your e-CNY wallet using Hong Kong FPS (Fast Payment System / 转数快):

Travelers had to set up Alipay or WeChat Pay, or carry cash. Open your existing PayPal app — no need to download WeChat or Alipay 2. Scan the merchant WeChat Pay QR code using PayPal scanner 3. Enter the amount and confirm payment 4. Funds come directly from your PayPal account — merchant receives Chinese yuan Alternatively, you can show your PayPal-generated QR code for the merchant to scan. Availability

en.rawContent:
一、必备证件（最重要）

- 必须携带：**护照原件**

- 复印件、- 。

---

## 二、三种购票方式（最简单）

### 方式1：12306 官方APP（推荐）
1. 下载“铁路12306”
2. 右上角切换 **English**
3. 注册 → 上传护照信息页
4. 选择出发地、目的地、日期
5. 选择高铁 G/D/C 字头列车
6. 支付：微信 / 支付宝 / Visa/Mastercard

【配图位置】12306英文界面、护照上传页

### 方式2：高铁站人工窗口
直接说：

- I want a ticket from ____ to ____.

- High-speed train, second class.

【配图位置】售票窗口、人工服务台
很坎坷
### 方式3：携程 / Trip.com（英文友好）
无需核验，外国信用卡可直接支付。

---

## 三、座位类型（一看就懂）

- **Second Class 二等座**：经济实惠，最推荐

- **First Class 一等座**：空间更大、更舒适

- **Business Class 商务座**：可平躺，豪华舒适

【配图位置】二等座、一等座、商务座实拍图

---

## 四、进站乘车全流程（一步一步）

### 1. 进入车站 → 安检

- 行李过机

- 人过安检门

- 液体、充电宝需单独检查

【配图位置】高铁站安检口

### 2. 实名制验证（刷护照）

- 护照放在闸机感应区

- 无法识别 → 走**人工通道**

【配图位置】自助闸机、人工通道

### 3. 查看大屏幕，找检票口
查看信息：

- Train No. 车次

- Gate 检票口（A/B）

- Time 时间

【配图位置】车站信息大屏

### 4. 检票上车

- 开车前 **10–15分钟** 开始检票

- 刷护照通行

【配图位置】检票闸机

### 5. 找车厢 → 找座位

- Car 01 / 02… 车厢号

- A/F 靠窗

- C/D 靠过道

【配图位置】车厢号、座位号标识

---

## 五、车上服务（超实用）

- 每个座位都有 **充电口**

- 车厢连接处有 **免费热水**

- 二维码点餐，直接送到座位

- 卫生间干净，有卫生纸

- 换乘：跟着 **Transfer** 指示走，不用出站

【配图位置】充电口、热水机、点餐二维码

---

## 六、出站流程
1. 下车跟随 **Exit** 出口指示
2. 刷护照出站
3. 完成！
/。。。hi那你就哦你
---

## 七、必看重要提醒
1. 护照 = 车票，**不用取纸质票**
2. 姓名必须与护照**完全一致**
3. 大站建议**提前60分钟**到站
4. G/D/C 是高铁；K/T/Z 是普通火车
5. 禁止携带：刀具、易燃品、超大液体
6. 车上保持安静，不食用异味食品

---

## 八、实用英文短句（直接照着说）

- Where is security check? 安检在哪？

- Where is Gate ____? ____检票口在哪？

- I need help with my ticket. 我需要票务帮助。

- Can I use the manual channel? 我可以走人工通道吗？

- Where is transfer? 换乘怎么走？

- Where is the toilet? 卫生间在哪？

---

购票 → 安检 → 验证护照 → 候车 → 检票 → 上车 → 乘车 → 出站
